evidence: naip-source-dates.json; source fetcher selects every NAIP item in the latest acquisition year; source IDs are not embedded in raster tags
finding: Four 2021 NAIP items are reconstructed: two dated 2021-11-21 and two dated 2021-09-24. A single mosaic therefore combines late-fall and early-fall acquisitions across different footprints. Contact-sheet windows show extensive snow-like bright cover in parts of Park City.
confidence: high for STAC candidates and dates; medium for exact source mosaic assignment; qualitative for snow cover
action: Acquire aligned, verified snow-free imagery for obscured corridors; retain current 2021 imagery as a separate winter/late-fall evaluation slice. Avoid blending dates without scene-level provenance.

evidence: contact_sheet_01.png and contact_sheet_02.png; RGB, NIR/R/G, relief shown without vector/prediction overlays
finding: Many sampled windows show snow-like or very bright low-texture cover, while a smaller subset shows exposed ground/canopy, deep shadow, or invalid coverage. Brightness alone cannot distinguish snow from rock, pavement, cloud, or roof. No corridor-level snow fraction was independently traced.
confidence: exploratory visual screen only; not a verified snow label
action: Manually trace visible snow at both window and reference-corridor scale; preserve snow, mixed, bare, shadow, canopy, bright non-snow, invalid, and unknown strata.

evidence: audit_samples.csv image_mask_valid_fraction computed from tile masks
finding: 17/45 windows have under 99% valid image-mask coverage; 8/45 are under 50%; 5/45 are under 10%. Park City and Corner Canyon include nearly or fully invalid edge crops. confidence: high for sampled tile-mask fractions and observed split availability; local tile pixel identity versus regenerated A tiles is not verified
action: Exclude invalid pixels from all image/weather denominators; keep these as coverage diagnostics, not weather failures. Regenerate A tiles on Kaggle for the trusted sample.
